question.problem: Consider the data sets $x$ and $y$ such that $\text{Cov}(x,y)=-6$ and their standard deviations are ${\sigma }_{x}=2$ and ${\sigma }_{y}=5.$ Compute the corresponding linear correlation coefficient.

current_example.problem:
Consider the following data sets:

$$
x = \big\{ 6, \: 3, \: -1, \: 0 \big\},\qquad
y = \big\{ 5, \: 7, \: -2, \: 6 \big\}
$$

You're given that $\overline{x}=2,$ $\overline{y}=4,$ $\sigma_x \approx 2.739,$ and $\sigma_y \approx 3.536.$ Calculate the corresponding linear correlation coefficient. Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
current_example.worked_solution:
The (population) linear correlation coefficient of the data sets $x=\big\{ x_1,x_2, \ldots, x_n \big\}$ and $y=\big\{ y_1,y_2, \ldots, y_n \big\}$ is given by 

$$
\rho(x,y) =  \dfrac{\textrm{Cov}(x,y)}{\sigma_x \cdot \sigma_y}
$$

where $\textrm{Cov}(x,y)$ is the covariance, and $\sigma_x$ and $\sigma_y$ are the standard deviations of the data sets.

First, we need to compute the covariance:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(6-2)(5-4)+(3-2)(7-4)+(-1-2)(-2-4)+(0-2)(6-4)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(4)(1)+(1)(3)+(-3)(-6)+(-2)(2)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[4+3+18-4] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 21 \\  & =5.25\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we use the formula. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho (x,y) & =\frac{\text{Cov}(x,y)}{{\sigma }_{x}\cdot {\sigma }_{y}} \\  & ≈\frac{5.25}{2.739\cdot 3.536} \\  & ≈0.54\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
